A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Open-MeDe under the same title and authorship. Their complete main texts and appendices A-D are readable, and equations, tables and figures can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original Open-MeDe recognition experiments, component and optimization analyses, computational measurements and qualitative visualizations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds component ablations, a sampling control, class-wise results and another qualitative example.

M1.justification: The support/query procedure, losses, first-order meta-optimization and Gaussian averaging remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithm 1. The revised averaging expression does not alter the implemented update in Equation (13) or the already stated exclusion of initial CLIP weights.

E1.justification: Both versions use K400, K600, UCF101, HMDB51, SSv2 and the same SCUBA/HAT scenarios. The added class-wise analysis and Golf Swing example examine existing UCF-SCUBA coverage rather than introducing a dataset or task.

E2.justification: New Table 7 explicitly compares meta-optimization-only and GWA-only variants against full Open-MeDe. The established benchmark and static-debiasing comparator sets remain unchanged, including X-CLIP, Open-VCLIP and FROSTER in Table 3.

E3.justification: V2 adds component on/off controls and a sampler selecting semantically similar classes across support/query batches (Appendix B.1, Tables 7 and 10). Settings for retained experiments, including splits, backbone, training budgets, preprocessing, metrics and inference views, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds a joint component ablation, extends the existing shuffle analysis with semantic sampling, and introduces a 22-class performance analysis and Golf Swing attention case. These provide additional component-attribution and failure evidence within the retained experimental framework.

E5.justification: The mean/standard-deviation reporting across validation splits and the three randomly sampled K600 class splits are retained. V2 introduces no new run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and matched appendix scores are unchanged. New Table 7 reports meta-only UCF/UCF-SCUBA accuracies of 83.2/32.1 and GWA-only accuracies of 82.3/30.7. Table 10 adds the similar-sampler results of 82.7/30.9, while Figure 5 reports gains over Open-VCLIP in 19 of 22 classes.

T1.justification: Equation (11) re-expresses weighted averaging using alpha coefficients, and normalization is made explicit. Both versions already exclude initial CLIP weights from GWA and retain the same Gaussian definition and recursive update. No substantive assumption, derivation, theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The introduction changes the description from a novel framework to the first meta-learning framework with static debiasing for this setting. Section 2.2 also adds an explicit first-integration claim for mini-batch training and meta-learning. The main performance and contribution claims otherwise remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix B.1 adds interpretations of component complementarity and a hypothesis that semantic sampling increases inter-task distribution shifts. The class-wise analysis attributes gains to localized dynamics and identifies weaknesses involving team sports or rapid spatial movement. The existing Appendix D limitations are retained.

D1.justification: The v2 abstract newly states that code is released and provides a repository link; v1 has no equivalent access statement. Hardware, preprocessing, hyperparameters and training details are retained. The PDFs establish the added disclosure, not the repository's contents or accessibility.

R1.justification: V2 adds three cited works, including Li et al. on meta-learning for domain generalization, mentions domain adaptation, and refines its comparison with MVSGG. It also strengthens priority positioning through explicit first-framework and first-integration claims. The broader related-work discussion remains stable.

P1.justification: There are localized wording edits in related work and method explanations, shortened CLIP preliminaries, standardized UCF-SCUBA terminology, additional analysis paragraphs and revised acknowledgments. The main section sequence and appendix A-D organization remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 7 and Figures 5 and 8, expands and reformats the sampler table, and adds a Venue column to Table 1. Figure 2 is lightly revised and relocated. Other figures and tables largely retain their displays while shifting position or numbering.

improvement.justification: The added component and sampler controls strengthen evidence about why Open-MeDe works, while the class-wise analysis makes its failure boundaries more specific. The code-access disclosure improves reproducibility information. These are bounded gains over v1: the main results remain unchanged, and the added mechanism explanations are still partly speculative.
